posts.text: 🇬🇳 🇧🇫 ⚡ - BREAKING: "The military option is on the table. The lackey [Ibrahim Traore of Burkina Faso] of Russafrique [a derogatory term calling Traore a puppet of Russia, a play on the word 'Francafrique'] has been warned. The provocations against Guinea and Conakry must stop very quickly. From now on, we will ensure respect for the rules and for our country," - Mamady Doumbouya, President of Guinea. Note: Relations between Burkina Faso and Guinea, countries ruled by juntas, have reached a boiling point. The crisis erupted on November 2 when Doumbouya banned unlicensed artisanal gold mining in northeastern Guinea, hitting hubs like Siguiri. Officially, Conakry cited environmental damage. In reality, Doumbouya is moving to formalize the gold sector, curb cross-border smuggling (which includes into Mali and Burkina Faso), and capture state revenues. Siguiri's mines employed tens of thousands of Burkinabè workers—over 45,000 have already been forced to return home after deadly clashes left at least 10 dead and over 1,200 arrested. In response, Ibrahim Traore—who campaigns on fiery anti-imperialism but seems to be completely fine with the extractive imperialism of Burkina Faso's resources by Russia, China, the UAE, and Turkey—ramped up state propaganda against Conakry. After Burkina Faso's state broadcaster, RTB, aired a caricature mocking Doumbouya, Guinea banned RTB nationwide and accused Ouagadougou of trying to drive a wedge between Conakry and fellow AES states Mali and Niger.

Israeli caretaker Defense Minister Israel Katz says Iran is "in the process of developing chemical weapons" and that Israel "will not allow" it, repeating a claim Netanyahu has used to push for renewed attacks on Iran. Katz did not say how far the alleged program has progressed or present any evidence, but said Israeli and US plans for a joint strike are ready and "Trump will decide." Iran denies the claim and calls it "fraudulent." Some US officials reportedly see the Israeli intelligence as a pressure campaign and have compared it to the US intelligence claims on Iraq before the 2003 invasion, which said Iraq held weapons of mass destruction.

🇺🇸 💻 First the FBI, now the CIA: hackers strike US intelligence The CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI), which oversees 17 US intelligence agencies, have suffered a cybersecurity breach affecting their open-source intelligence analysis system, US media reported. The compromised network is used to analyze satellite imagery, commercial databases, social media content and other publicly available information. Data from other government agencies may also have been exposed. Officials insist no classified information was compromised, but the full extent of the breach and the identity of those responsible remain unclear. The incident adds to a growing list of US government cybersecurity incidents and technological failures: 🌏 Two separate breaches at the FBI, including an apparent hack of its nationwide criminal information database 🌏 Department of Agriculture's farmer payment system hit by a cyberattack 🌏 Pentagon and Department of Homeland Security affected by cybersecurity incidents 🌏 NSA’s internal classified network knocked offline for days, reportedly due to a technical problem Earlier, more than 50 leaders in government, business, AI and cybersecurity told Axios that cyberattacks against US businesses and critical infrastructure are expected to become increasingly frequent , sophisticated and disruptive over the next 18 months. 👍 Substack | Chat | @geopolitics_prime
